raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A cold `/v1/decisions` request can prefill the same input once per question. The engine already supports MIS query sharing and Qwen3.5/3.8 GDN state branching from #33922, but the decisions route rejects `--enable-mis` and submits full prompts as separate items.

## Modifications

- Pack the questions' common token prefix as the MIS query and their remaining tokens as independent items. Preserve per-question labels, temperature, raw label mass and caller order. Keep the ordinary path unchanged.
- Check the complete packed prefill budget and reject images and speculative decoding. Keep the existing System One behavior. `usage.prompt_tokens` reports the packed sequence.
- Propagate MIS positions to the mRoPE tensor consumed by Qwen3.5/3.8. Empty-query delimiters receive a valid dummy position, avoiding an invalid fused-RoPE lookup.
- Extend the existing CPU suites and document the opt-in behavior and limits. No new GDN kernels or cache support.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Render question prompts] --> B[Common prefix + question tails]
    B --> C[Existing MIS score request]
    C --> D[Item-relative positions + mRoPE]
    D --> E[Shared query prefill + independent GDN branches]
    E --> F[Per-question label scores]
```

## Accuracy Tests

Validation covers the serving contract on a fixed synthetic workload:

- `test_serving_decisions.py`: **30 passed**; `test_gdn_mis_metadata.py`: **5 passed**.
- Existing `test_qwen35_gdn_multi_item_scoring.py`, with the pinned **Qwen3.8-27B** checkpoint: **3 passed**, including empty queries, sibling changes/reordering and concurrent requests.
- Negative controls reproduce the original MIS refusal and wrong mRoPE coordinates. Removing the empty-query clamp reproduces the invalid RoPE index; the final long empty-query replay returns 200 with finite scores.
- `/v1/decisions` equals manually packed `/v1/score` exactly. Changing a sibling's contents without changing its shape leaves the other rows bit-identical.
- Additional GPU edge checks cover single/identical questions, concurrency, image and oversized-input refusals, and valid requests after errors. These exercise unchanged no-speculation/nonempty-prefix paths; final-commit API parity, content isolation and the long empty-query replay were executed again.

**Scores are not numerically interchangeable with the original prompts.** All eight top-scoring labels matched on the main workload, but normalized probabilities differed by up to **0.152**; separate single-question probes reached **0.191** because the prefix split changes. Expected numeric scores can therefore change too.

A fixed-query packed-versus-single check measured **0.02236** with the default BF16 readout, failing an initially chosen 0.02 normalized bound. That bound was incorrectly derived from #33922's **unnormalized** score test; it is not presented as passing. BF16 logit steps amplify small layout differences. With the existing FP32 LM-head flag, the measured maximum was **0.01270**. An independent, unchanged SIS reference with an FP32 head moved **0.02500** when only prefill chunking changed. These are measurements, not accuracy or determinism guarantees. No test tolerance was relaxed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One NVIDIA GB300, TP=1, Qwen3.8-27B revision `1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`, BF16 weights/KV and FP32 GDN state. Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. Eight questions share 3,985 tokens. Both arms disable radix caching, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs; concurrency 1, three kernel warmups, ten measured HTTP round trips, zero errors.

| Mode | Median complete-request latency | Computed tokens | Cached tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SIS, base `456231e251` | 1217.5 ms | 32,155 | 0 |
| MIS, this change | 320.0 ms | 4,269 | 0 |

**3.81× faster on this workload, with 86.7% fewer computed tokens.** The API input is the same; MIS delimiter semantics differ as described above. The final profile records 48 `_forward_extend_mis` calls and 96 `_forward_mis_segments` calls: one query phase and one item phase for each GDN layer.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the measured workload</summary>

Run the base without `--enable-mis`, and the candidate with it, on the same GPU. All other settings are the same:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --revision 1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0 \
  --served-model-name qwen38-decisions --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31500 \
  --tp 1 --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --context-length 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --enable-mis
```

```python
import statistics
import time
import requests

state = "\n".join(
    f"[{i:03d}] customer: order #{4400 + i} "
    f"{'was charged twice' if i % 5 == 0 else 'shows as shipped but has not arrived'}; "
    f"agent: we escalated to {'billing' if i % 5 == 0 else 'logistics'} "
    f"and will update within {(i % 4) + 1} business days."
    for i in range(110)
)
questions = [{'id': 'team',
  'type': 'choice',
  'question': 'Which team should own this thread?',
  'options': [{'name': 'billing'}, {'name': 'logistics'}, {'name': 'technical'}]},
 {'id': 'refund', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Does any customer ask for a refund?'},
 {'id': 'urgency',
  'type': 'score',
  'question': 'How urgent is the thread?',
  'levels': ['low', 'medium', 'high']},
 {'id': 'escalate', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Should a supervisor review this thread?'},
 {'id': 'sentiment',
  'type': 'score',
  'question': 'Overall customer sentiment',
  'levels': ['angry', 'upset', 'neutral', 'happy']},
 {'id': 'channel',
  'type': 'choice',
  'question': 'Which channel is this?',
  'options': [{'name': 'email'}, {'name': 'chat'}, {'name': 'phone'}]},
 {'id': 'fraud', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Is there any sign of fraud?'},
 {'id': 'resolved', 'type': 'yes_no', 'question': 'Is every issue in the thread resolved?'}]
payload = {
    "model": "qwen38-decisions", "input": state, "questions": questions,
    "return_prompt_token_ids": False,
}
session = requests.Session()
latencies = []
for i in range(13):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    response = session.post("http://127.0.0.1:31500/v1/decisions", json=payload, timeout=240)
    elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    response.raise_for_status()
    if i >= 3:
        latencies.append(elapsed_ms)
print("median ms:", statistics.median(latencies))
print("usage:", response.json()["usage"])
```

</details>

This is a **cold, text-only prototype**. MIS disables warm prefix reuse server-wide. Use a dedicated scoring server without speculative decoding; mixed generation traffic is not supported. The validated 32K prefill envelope stays below the inherited 65,535-token per-item MIS limit. Clef's trained joint-head path is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on the exact candidate.
- [x] Focused CPU regressions and real Qwen3.8 GPU checks passed.
- [x] Documentation updated; Mintlify build and link checks passed.
- [x] Measured latency, dispatch and numerical limitations recorded.
- [ ] Upstream CI has not been requested.

 ## Thinking models
 
@@ -205,6 +206,17 @@ Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B think by default. `/v1/decisions` turns thinking
 
 These models mix full and linear attention. Answer probabilities can move by up to several hundredths (0.07 in our checks), and `label_mass` by up to about 0.14, between cold and prefix-cached requests and across batch compositions, while the chosen option stayed the same in our checks. On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `--disable-radix-cache` gave identical values across sequential repeats, at the cost of prefix reuse.
 
+## Score questions over one shared prefix
+
+The prompts of a request's questions start with the same chat template header and input. Without `--enable-mis`, a cold request can compute that shared part once per question, although prompts that chunked prefill moves to a later batch can reuse it from the radix cache. A server launched with `--enable-mis` and `--attention-backend flashinfer`, plus `--linear-attn-prefill-backend triton` on hybrid models such as Qwen3.8-27B, and without speculative decoding, scores all questions of a request as one multi-item sequence instead. The sequence holds the longest token prefix that every prompt shares, then each question's remaining tokens as an item after a delimiter token, and every item keeps at least the last token of its prompt. In full-attention layers, an item's tokens see the shared prefix and their own item, but not the delimiter. The linear-attention layers of hybrid models continue each item from their state after the shared prefix and read its delimiter first. No layer lets one question see another.
+
+- Dedicate the server to scoring. `--enable-mis` turns off the radix cache, chunked prefill, and CUDA graphs for the whole server, so a repeated input is computed again. Do not send chat or `/generate` requests to it: a prefill batch that mixes them with multi-item scoring requests fails an assertion.
+- Probabilities differ from those of a server without `--enable-mis`, because each answer is read inside the packed sequence. On one Qwen3.8-27B request in BF16 with eight questions over a 3,985-token shared prefix, probabilities moved by up to 0.152 from scoring each original prompt alone, and every question kept its top-scoring label. Where an item sits in the sequence also matters: identical questions in one request, or a question after reordering, differed by up to about 0.03. These are measurements of one workload, not bounds. With `--enable-fp32-lm-head`, `/v1/score` requests that kept the same shared query and question tails moved by less than 0.013 when a tail was scored alone, reordered, or placed next to a changed tail. A `/v1/decisions` request with one question splits its prompt at a different point, so that result does not cover it.
+- `prompt_token_ids` holds the shared prefix, the delimiter, and the question's remaining tokens. To reproduce the answers exactly through `/v1/score` on the same server, send the shared prefix as `query` and the remaining tokens of every question, in request order, as `items`. Sending `prompt_token_ids` with an empty `query`, or one question alone, packs the tokens differently and can change the probabilities.
+- `usage.prompt_tokens` counts the scored sequence: the shared prefix once, the remaining tokens of every question, and one delimiter per question plus one.
+- The scored sequence must fit one prefill, below the context length minus reserved tokens, below the scheduler's input limit, and within `--max-prefill-tokens`. A longer request returns 400. Multi-item attention stores positions within an item as 16-bit values, so a question's remaining tokens must not exceed 65,535. The server does not check this separately; the limits above keep every item shorter unless `--max-prefill-tokens` is above 65,535.
+- Requests with images return 400. On `/v1/systemone`, generation models and decision checkpoints refuse the server.
+
 ## System One compatible API
 
 `POST /v1/systemone` serves the same decisions in the request and response shape of the System One API, with a `state`, a map of `noul`, `choice`, and `score` questions keyed by your ids, and one answer per id. Clients written for that API, including the official TypeSafe SDKs, get decisions by pointing their base URL at the server, with the exceptions listed below. For ordinary generation models, the route uses the same rendering, label checks, and scoring as `/v1/decisions`, and refuses the same servers, chat templates, and prompts, listed in [Errors](#errors). Its request fields are checked as described below. A decision checkpoint such as [PPLX-Decider-v1-27B](/cookbook/autoregressive/Perplexity/PPLX-Decider-v1-27B) instead gets the prompt, answer codes, and calibrated temperature it was trained with. When its `decision_config.json` sets `attention_mode` to `noncausal_full_attention`, as [PPLX-Decider-v1.1-27B](/cookbook/autoregressive/Perplexity/PPLX-Decider-v1.1-27B) does, its full-attention layers read the whole prompt, and the server turns off the radix cache and chunked prefill, which would show those layers only part of it. A joint schema checkpoint such as [Clef](/cookbook/autoregressive/Cloudflare/clef) answers all questions from one prompt in one prefill, scored by its joint schema head, and does not use the chat template.
